operations.applied_qualified_row: | DS-MCU-072 | `datasheets/stmicroelectronics_stm32g031k8t6_rev4.md` | DS12992 Rev4 section3.5 Boot modes; section3.7.5 Reset mode; section4 Pinouts | Table11 reset qualifier; Table12 PA9/PA13/PA14 and footnotes2/3/5 | pp.15,19,35,38-39 | **Qualified reset/default facts only, not a whole pre-application safety proof.** For STM32G031K8T6, Table11 says I/Os are analog inputs upon reset unless otherwise specified. It does not establish the claimed universal MODER/PUPDR/OTYPER reset words, a universal no-pull state, or persistence throughout ROM/startup/application handover. Table12 fn5 resets PA13/PA14 to SWD alternate functions with internal pull-up/pull-down respectively; fn2 makes PC13/14/15 functions depend on RTC registers not reset by system reset; fn3 gives PF2-NRST default NRST functionality. Section3.7.5 disables I/O Schmitt triggers during/upon exiting reset and deactivates the NRST built-in pull-up for an internal reset source; neither statement proves general output high-Z through boot. Section3.5 permits user Flash/system-memory/SRAM boot, describes empty-main-Flash forcing to system memory under its stated condition, and states that the bootloader reconfigures some GPIOs out of high-Z (including listed USART interfaces PA9/PA10 or PA2/PA3; actual per-pad behavior needs applicable AN2606/manual/settings). **Actual PA9/U6 SHDN reset-to-application behavior, passive dominance and safety margin are UNKNOWN here.** No entire-window no-floating-pin assurance, R11 margin or ISS-015 disposition is supported by this source-only row. Applicable RM0444 versus legacy RM0454, exact register words, option bits/defaults and actual settings remain UNKNOWN. Legacy board consumers require separately scoped owner follow-up; no board fault, code fix or waiver is adjudicated. operations.old_public_row: | DS-MCU-073 | `datasheets/stmicroelectronics_stm32g031k8t6_rev-unknown.md` | **Table 2** ("STM32G031x4/x6/x8 device features and peripheral counts"); **Figure 7** ("STM32G031KxT LQFP32 pinout") and **Figure 9** ("STM32G031CxT LQFP48 pinout"); **Table 12** ("Pin assignment and description") | Table 2; Table 12 (PB10/PB11/PA11/PA12 rows) | pp. 12, 33, 35, 36–39 of DS12992 Rev 4 | **HIGH confidence, directly re-derived from ST's own primary datasheet this session** (fetched and read live via `r.jina.ai` text-extraction proxy against `https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32g031k8.pdf` — the same primary document DS-MCU-050 through DS-MCU-053/062 already cite): **PB10 and PB11 are NOT bonded out on the LQFP32/UFQFPN32 package** (STM32G031K8T6's actual package) — Table 2 lists only 30 GPIOs for the K-suffix package vs. 44 for the C-suffix (LQFP48/UFQFPN48) package; Figure 7's full 32-pad LQFP32 pinout diagram does not list PB10 or PB11 anywhere, while Figure 9's LQFP48 diagram explicitly does; Table 12's own PB10/PB11 rows show a dash (not present) in the LQFP32/UFQFPN32 column and a real pin number (22, 23 respectively) only in the LQFP48/UFQFPN48 column. **PA11 and PA12 ARE bonded out on LQFP32/UFQFPN32** and carry **I2C2_SCL**/**I2C2_SDA** respectively as an AF6 alternate function (Table 12's PA11[PA9] and PA12[PA10] rows, LQFP32/UFQFPN32 column = pin 22/23–24 depending on the part's pin-remap option-byte state; both rows list "...I2C2_SCL"/"...I2C2_SDA" among their alternate functions). Independently cross-corroborated via a second, differently-sourced primary-equivalent record: ST's own CubeMX pin database as consumed by `stm32duino/Arduino_Core_STM32`'s auto-generated `PeripheralPins.c` for this exact part/package family (`variants/STM32G0xx/G031K(4-6-8)(T-U)_G041K(6-8)(T-U)/PeripheralPins.c`, CubeMX DB release 6.0.180) — its `PinMap_I2C_SCL`/`PinMap_I2C_SDA` tables list only `{PA_9, PA_9_R, PA_11, PB_6, PB_8}`/`{PA_10, PA_10_R, PA_12, PB_7, PB_9}` respectively, and PB10/PB11 appear in zero of its ADC/I2C/TIM/UART/SPI pin-map tables at all. **Corrects/supersedes DS-MCU-052's implicit assumption** that PB10/PB11 are accessible LQFP-32 pins (DS-MCU-052 correctly identified the *peripheral* — I2C2, not I2C1 — but neither DS-MCU-052 nor the original Rev 2 review that produced it separately checked pin-level package bonding). Basis for `validation/open-issues.md` **ISS-026** (CRITICAL) and its recommended fix (re-route the IMU I2C bus to PA11/PA12) | Hardware Lead (independent verification, prompted by a human-relayed finding from a parallel KiCad-conversion session) | 2026-09-09 |
